notes.meaning: Speaking softly and calmly can quiet someone who is furious, just like a gentle rain calms a storm. But speaking with harsh, insulting words stirs up trouble and makes anger explode. A gentle answer protects peace when tensions are high.

A wise person knows how to share the truth in an attractive and helpful way at the right time. In contrast, fools blurt out nonsense without thinking, gushing foolish words like an overflowing fountain.

God sees everything that happens across the entire earth, observing both wicked and good deeds. Nothing can be hidden in secret from His eyes. This brings comfort to the upright while warning those doing wrong that their actions are known.
Words that bring healing and peace bring life and refreshment to others, like fruit from a healthy tree. On the other hand, twisted and dishonest speech wounds people deeply and breaks their spirit.
A person acts foolishly when they refuse to listen to a father's guidance and discipline. Taking correction seriously shows true good sense and leads to wisdom.
God blesses the home of the righteous with lasting treasure, including inner peace and contentment. But even when the wicked gain great wealth, their dishonest income brings only worry and trouble.
Wise people freely share helpful truth wherever they go, helping everyone who listens. Fools cannot do this because their hearts are empty of good wisdom.

Religious rituals and sacrifices mean nothing to God if the person offering them continues to live in wicked rebellion. God delights instead in the simple, sincere prayer of those who desire to do right.
The Lord hates not only the false worship of evil people, but the whole direction of their daily lives. In contrast, He deeply loves those who persistently pursue goodness and obedience.
When someone wanders away from God's right path, corrective discipline feels severe and painful to them. If they stubbornly refuse all correction, their path ends in destruction and death.
The realm of the dead and the place of destruction lie completely open to God's sight. Since God sees the hidden depths of the grave, He certainly knows every secret thought in the human heart.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that Sheol in the Old Testament originally referred to a shadowy realm for all the dead, distinct from the later Christian concept of hell.

notes.meaning: A proud mocker hates being told when he is wrong. Because he cannot stand criticism or look honestly at his own mistakes, he avoids spending time with wise people who might correct him.
When a person has inner joy and peace, it naturally brightens their face. But deep inner grief and heartache wear a person down and break their spirit.
A person with understanding is hungry to learn more and keeps searching for divine truth. A fool, however, is satisfied with foolishness and feeds on it like daily bread.

When someone is crushed by constant sorrow and gloom, every day feels heavy and bitter. But a person with a cheerful, contented heart enjoys life as if attending a nonstop feast, no matter their circumstances.
Having only a modest income along with reverence for God brings quiet peace and contentment. Great wealth without God often brings anxiety, conflict, and a troubled conscience.
A simple, inexpensive meal of vegetables shared in a home filled with love is far sweeter than the finest feast. An expensive banquet filled with anger and hatred brings only misery.
A person with a quick temper easily starts arguments and fans the flames of conflict. A patient person who controls their anger cools down arguments and restores peace.

A lazy person constantly invents excuses and sees obstacles everywhere, as if their path were blocked with sharp thorns. Diligent, upright people face their duties, finding a smooth and open road before them.
A son who chooses wisdom brings deep gladness to his father's heart. But a foolish person acts selfishly, showing disrespect and contempt for the mother who loved and raised him.
Someone who lacks good judgment actually finds pleasure in doing foolish and sinful things. A person with true understanding keeps their life aligned with what is right and walks straight ahead.
Rushing into decisions without seeking advice often leads to disappointment and failure. Consulting multiple wise and thoughtful advisers gives plans the guidance they need to succeed.
Giving an answer that is both helpful and spoken at the right moment brings great joy. Speaking the right words at just the right time is a wonderful blessing to those who hear.
Wise people follow an upward course of life, setting their desires on higher, godly things. This path protects them from the destructive road below that leads down to the grave.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some commentators understand this verse primarily as a promise of avoiding premature physical death on earth rather than as an explicit reference to heaven.

notes.meaning: The Lord brings ruin on the proud and powerful who exploit others and think they are safe. At the same time, He defends the defenseless, protecting the land and boundary markers of the vulnerable widow.
God hates evil plans and selfish schemes even before they turn into actions. In contrast, kind and sincere words are delightful and pure in His sight.
A person driven by greed who chases dishonest money brings distress and trouble upon their own family. But someone who hates bribes and unfair gain protects their household and lives safely.
Righteous people pause to think carefully before they speak so their words do good rather than harm. Evil people do not consider the consequences and rush to blurt out hurtful talk.
The Lord remains far from those who defy Him and live wickedly, withholding His favor and help. But He draws near and listens attentively to the sincere prayers of those who seek to do His will.
Seeing a cheerful face or looking upon the pleasant sights of God's world brings joy to the heart. In the same way, receiving good news refreshes a person's inner being and brings health to the body.
A person who willingly listens to life-giving correction shows true wisdom. Such people naturally feel at home among the wise and learn from their company.
Those who refuse instruction and guidance harm themselves, acting as if their own lives had no value. But anyone who accepts correction gains good sense and grows in understanding.
Reverence for the Lord is the true foundation and school of wisdom. Before a person can receive lasting honor, they must first learn to walk in genuine humility before God and others.
